Packed spatial indexes

Source: R/index.R
geo_rtree.Rd

geo_rtree() packs each geometry's box into a static R-tree, and geo_kdtree() packs points into a static k-d tree (design section 6.8). Both are immutable, bulk-loaded and held as one raw vector in flatbush's and kdbush's serialised formats, so geo_index_raw() gives bytes that flatbush and kdbush in JavaScript and geo-index in Rust and Python load unchanged, and geo_index_from_raw() reads such bytes back, checking them first.

Usage

geo_rtree(x, node_size = 16L, lossy = c("error", "warn", "allow"))

geo_kdtree(x, node_size = 64L)

geo_index_raw(index)

geo_index_from_raw(raw)

Arguments

x

A geo_vctr or a geo_extent for geo_rtree(); a geo_vctr of points for geo_kdtree().

node_size

Entries per node, 2 to 65535: flatbush's default of 16 for R-trees and kdbush's 64 for k-d trees.

lossy

As for geo_box().

index

A zugeo_index.

raw

A raw vector holding a flatbush or kdbush index.

Value

geo_rtree(), geo_kdtree() and geo_index_from_raw(): a zugeo_index. geo_index_raw(): a raw vector.

Details

Null and empty geometries are left out of an index, and queries return positions in the vector the index was built from. An index read from raw bytes numbers its items 1 to n in the order they were added.

See also

geo_query_box() for queries and joins.

Examples

x <- geo_points(c(0, 5, 9), c(0, 5, 9))
tree <- geo_rtree(x)
geo_query_box(tree, geo_extent(4, 4, 10, 10))
#> [1] 2 3
bytes <- geo_index_raw(tree)
geo_query_box(geo_index_from_raw(bytes), geo_extent(4, 4, 10, 10))
#> [1] 2 3
